title: `platformSetupContextDirectoryOverlay` should be skipped when `--isolation=chroot` is set
body:
### Issue Description

I am having issues running `buildah` in my CI environment.
- Gitlab Kubernetes Executor
- EKS with EC2 on AL2023
- buildah version 1.44.0 (via Nix)

After a lot of debugging with some assistance from Claude, I've generated the following summary of what I think is going on.

---

### Problem

When running `buildah build --isolation=chroot --storage-driver=vfs` inside a Kubernetes pod (GitLab Kubernetes executor, EKS, cgroupv2, AL2023 kernel 6.1), the build fails before any Dockerfile steps execute:
Error: mounting an overlay over build context directory: creating overlay scaffolding
for build context directory: mount overlay:/var/tmp/buildah-context-xxx/overlay/xxx/merge,
data: lowerdir=/builds/myproject,upperdir=.../upper,workdir=.../work,userxattr: invalid argument
The pod runs on an overlay rootfs (containerd snapshots) without /dev/fuse access. The kernel rejects the userxattr overlay mount with EINVAL.

### Root Cause

`platformSetupContextDirectoryOverlay` in `imagebuildah/build.go` is called unconditionally before any Dockerfile stage is parsed. It attempts to mount an overlay over the build context directory regardless of `--isolation` or `--storage-driver` flags. These are separate code paths — `--storage-driver=vfs` controls image layer storage via `containers/storage` but has no effect on the build context overlay, which uses `pkg/overlay.MountWithOptions` directly.

### Why This Is Unexpected

Both `--isolation=chroot` and `--storage-driver=vfs` signal that the caller has opted out of overlayfs machinery — either because the environment doesn't support it or because they've explicitly chosen simpler semantics. The build context overlay ignores both signals.
Chroot isolation specifically does not benefit from CoW semantics over the build context the way rootless isolation does. Skipping `platformSetupContextDirectoryOverlay` when `--isolation=chroot` is set would be consistent with the existing opt-out semantics of that flag.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `buildah build --isolation=chroot --storage-driver=vfs` inside a Kubernetes pod where:

  - The pod rootfs is an overlay mount (standard containerd setup)
  - `/dev/fuse` is not available (no FUSE device plugin)
  - cgroupv2 eBPF device filtering is active

2. Observe failure before STEP 1 executes

### Debugging Notes

- Setting `BUILDAH_ISOLATION=chroot` via environment variable has no effect — the error occurs in the Nix-packaged binary's startup sequence before flags are parsed
- `--storage-driver=vfs` has no effect on the context overlay — confirmed via source inspection that these are separate code paths
- No` containers.conf` option or environment variable exists to disable `platformSetupContextDirectoryOverlay`
-The issue does not reproduce with apt buildah 1.33.7 (Ubuntu noble), which predates the build context overlay feature introduced in the 1.34–1.38 range
-Workarounds tried: `--no-pivot`, `BUILDAH_TMPDIR=/tmp`, copying build context to `/tmp` — none affect the context overlay mount
- `privileged: true` on the pod resolves the issue by bypassing cgroupv2 device filtering, confirming the root cause is `/dev/fuse` access

Related ### Issues

[#4715](https://github.com/containers/buildah/issues/4715) — overlay mount failure in GitLab runner, similar environment constraints, predates the build context overlay feature but shows the same class of problem
[#4727](https://github.com/containers/buildah/issues/4727) — `userxattr` overlay error on overlay rootfs, same underlying kernel rejection
[#6116](https://github.com/containers/buildah/issues/6116) — fuse-overlayfs incompatibility in 1.39, related overlay machinery

comments.body: chroot isolation isn't specific to any storage driver, but I agree that we shouldn't be trying to use any overlays when we're not using an overlay storage driver.  https://github.com/podman-container-tools/buildah/pull/6126 is y attempt to fix that, but it is not passing all of the tests, so there's still work to be done there.
A friendly reminder that this issue had no activity for 30 days.

Another data point, from a platform with a different failure mode — plus a consequence I think raises the priority.

**Same break on OpenShift under the `restricted-v2` SCC** (GitLab Kubernetes executor, RHEL 9.6 kernel `5.14.0-570.117.1.el9_6`, `buildah build --isolation chroot --storage-driver vfs --storage-opt vfs.ignore_chown_errors=true`):

```
Error: mounting an overlay over build context directory: creating overlay scaffolding for
build context directory: mount overlay:/var/tmp/buildah-context-4251764731/overlay/1309175474/merge,
data: lowerdir=/tmp/ctx,upperdir=...,workdir=...,userxattr: invalid argument
```

Verified by compiling v1.45.0 from the release tarball and running it in a single-UID user namespace with no subuid/subgid ranges and `/proc/self/setgroups` = `deny`. v1.43.1 builds fine in the identical environment — `platformSetupContextDirectoryOverlay` doesn't exist there; it appears in v1.44.0 onward.

Two things to add to the thread:

**1. There are two distinct failure modes, and one of them defeats the workarounds in #6892.** Where the context directory sits on an overlay rootfs, the kernel rejects `lowerdir` + `userxattr` with `EINVAL` — the case reported here. But where the platform *forbids* unprivileged new-filesystem mounts (SELinux policy for `container_t` on our nodes: bind mounts pass, new filesystem mounts do not), the same call fails with `EPERM` regardless of where `upperdir`/`workdir` are placed. Relocating the scaffolding — `engine.image_copy_tmp_dir`, or mounting a host dir over `/var/tmp` — cannot help that class of environment, because it is the mount itself that is denied, not its location. Worth distinguishing the two when testing a fix.

**2. It transitively blocks the fix for #6947.** We filed #6947 (chroot isolation calling `setgroups()` in a namespace where it is denied, killing every `RUN` step); it was fixed in v1.45.0, thank you. But since the context overlay landed in v1.44.0 and has no flag, environment variable or `containers.conf` opt-out, *every release containing the #6947 fix is unbuildable for us*. The practical effect is a hard version ceiling: we stay on v1.43.1 with a locally maintained patch, and there is no newer version to move to — so this is not only an ergonomics regression, it also gates affected users out of subsequent fixes.

+1 to the direction in your comment above — skipping the context overlay when the storage driver is not overlay would resolve our case completely, and honouring `--isolation=chroot` would too. I see #6126 is still open and last touched in June; if it would help, we can run our reproduction against a build of that branch, since for us it is a one-command check.

One suggestion in case a full fix is awkward: `usingContextOverlay` is already threaded from `platformSetupContextDirectoryOverlay()` through `buildDockerfilesOnce()` into `newExecutor()`, so the non-overlay path appears to be supported already. Treating the mount as best-effort — log at debug level on failure and continue with `options.ContextDirectory` unchanged — might be a small change that unblocks every environment in this and the two sibling issues.
